declared.title: When Problem Solving Followed by Instruction Works: Evidence for Productive Failure
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « when problem solving followed by instruction works evidence for productive failure » (2026-11-23); line of research named in the idea scout's notes

population: 53 studies (166 comparisons) of students, comparing problem solving before instruction with instruction first

findings.text: Trying to solve a problem before being taught (and usually failing) led to better learning than being taught first

support.sentence: Our results showed a significant, moderate effect in favor of PS-I (Hedge's g 0.36 [95% confidence interval 0.20; 0.51]).

findings.text: For young pupils (grades 2 to 5) and for general skills, being taught first did better

support.sentence: Contrasting trends were, however, observed for younger age learners (second to fifth graders) and for the learning of domain-general skills, for which effect sizes favored I-PS.

limits: school learning, mostly mathematics and science; the failure is planned and always followed by teaching
quasi-experiments included; the bias-adjusted estimate (g 0.87) is larger than the raw one, unusual: not used
countries not given in the abstract (full text not read)
allegiance: Kapur created productive failure and promotes it
